title: Real-World Application Study to Evaluate the Use, Acceptance, and Perceived Benefits of the Medical Device FEMANEA Among Women with Stress and Mixed Incontinence
summary: Many women experience involuntary urine leakage when their bodies are under strain, such as when coughing, sneezing, or exercising. Pelvic floor exercises for at least three months are recommended. FEMANEA is an approved medical device that, among other things, provides digital guidance for such exercises at home over a 90-day period. This study examines how FEMANEA is accepted in everyday life: willingness to recommend it, ease of use, perceived benefits, and usage behavior/adherence. After 90 days of using FEMANEA, participants receive a one-time final questionnaire to gather feedback on their experiences with the program.

interventions.name: Observation group: FEMANEA users (single-arm study, no control group) receive a one-time final questionnaire after 90 days of using FEMANEA, in which their experiences with the product are assessed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Female
Age ≥ 18 years
Stress incontinence only or mixed incontinence with predominant stress symptoms (ICD-10: N39.3, N39.48)
Sufficient knowledge of German
Availability of technical requirements (Internet access and a browser-capable device)
Existence of informed, voluntary consent
Exclusion criteria:
Individuals for whom a contraindication exists in accordance with the intended use and instructions for use of FEMANEA are excluded.
